impulse:	no filtering - each output pixel equals some input pixel
linear:	linear interpolation between pixels
cubic:	smooth interpolation between pixels
Keys:	cubic a=.50, approximates sinc (*)
Simon:	cubic a=.75, continuous 2nd derivative (*)
Rifman:	cubic a=1.0, lots of sharpening (*)
Mitchell:	mix of sharpening and smoothing (*+)
Parzen:	approximating B-spline (+)
notch:	hides moiré patterns (+)
Lanczos4:	good for scaling down (*)
Lanczos6:	good for scaling down with some sharpening (*)
sinc4:	good for scaling down with a lot of sharpening (*)
(*) has negative lobes, can produce values that are outside the range of the input pixels.
(+) not interpolatory, changes pixels even when no movement.

description.plain_text: The GridWarp3 node enables the user to warp an input image via the use of spline lines in the form of a 2D grid. Control points and their tangents can be moved, animated and linked to trackers. The input is distorted according to the output type selected and the topology of the source and destination grids. Both warping and morphing can be accomplished with this node by keying warp and mix parameters. If there is no destination image provided, then the mix and warp parameters are ignored. The output is produced by warping images between the source and destination grids by the warp amount and mixing the warped source and destination images by the mix amount. The source image is warped from the source positions towards the destination positions by the warp amount (0 to 1 equals 0 to 100%). The destination image (if supplied) is warped from the destination positions towards the source positions by 1-warp. The results are then mixed based on the mix parameter (0 = source, 1 = destination, .5 = 50% of each).

The results are then mixed based on the mix parameter (0 = source, 1 = destination, .5 = 50% of each).
